newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: New Czech law won't ban NATO nuclear deployment.
newsitem.headline: New Czech law won't ban NATO nuclear deployment.

text.p: The Czech parliament's lower house on Friday approved a law on nuclear materials after removing a clause that would have banned the stationing of NATO weapons on Czech territory.

The law, which requires approval by the Senate upper chamber, establishes rules for development, import, production, transfer, ownership, storage and other activities connected with nuclear materials.

Athough it is aimed primarily at nuclear power, the parliament, in consideration of potential requirements for NATO membership, earlier this year dropped a clause from the draft that would have banned nuclear weapons.
In effect, the materials law would not present a barrier to any deployment of nuclear weapons agreed in an international treaty.
The issue of stationing NATO nuclear arms on the territory of future members in Eastern Europe is highly controversial, with Russia opposing any eastward expansion of the Western alliance.

The Czech republic is seen as among former Soviet satellites to join the Western security alliance first, along with Poland and Hungary. A decision on opening up membership is expected from a summit of NATO leaders in Madrid next July.
NATO has not yet said if new members would be required to host nuclear weapons -- a requirement for current members.
The United States recently said it would not want new members to deploy nuclear weapons as a condition for membership, a move interpreted as a concession to Russia.
Opinion polls show Czechs split on whether to join NATO, but a solid majority is opposed to deploying nuclear weapons after the country lived with them for years as a Soviet satellite.
The Soviets removed their troops and weapons after Prague's 1989 revolution over communism.
The Czech law also defines rules for the commercial use of nuclear power in connection with the new Temelin power station under construction close to the border with Austria.
The Czech Republic has one operating nuclear power plant at Dukovany in the southeast.
